title: Practice: keep the freezing temperature
vision: Find and repair a temperature summary that mistakes a real 0 °C reading for missing data.
explanation: Laws and generation strategies are authored in LawSpec. Only the implementation changes language.
news: Input generation must include meaningful boundary values such as a real zero reading.
contributions: A distinct-temperature summary, an input strategy that includes freezing and negative values, the actual shrunk failure [0], seed/path replay and a saved freezing regression. The repaired function retains zero while removing repeats; evidence is scoped to these examples and short generated lists.

star.salient: Input generation must include meaningful boundary values such as a real zero reading.
star.surprise: The summary passes every positive sample while silently deleting the freezing temperature.
star.story: A weather station needs a list of distinct temperatures it recorded. Positive samples hide a zero-removal bug; a wider recipe finds it, shrinking isolates [0], and a saved example protects the repair.

hints: A list containing only 0 records one real temperature. Should its summary be empty?
Trace the zero-removal operation separately from removing duplicates. Which one violates the summary’s purpose?
Keep the distinct-value operation and remove the filter that discards zero. Load solution shows the complete repair.

stages.title: Which temperatures did the station record?
story: A weather station records temperatures as whole degrees Celsius. We want a summary of which temperatures occurred, with one copy of each value. The summary’s order does not matter. Repeated readings of 2 °C should produce one 2; a reading of 0 °C must still appear. Negative temperatures are valid too. You will use a small generated failure to locate a mistake and keep it as a regression.

This differs from the library queue: equal ranks represented separate requests there. Here we deliberately summarize distinct values rather than preserve how many times each temperature occurred. The original readings are the input; this function returns a summary.

unique in Solution first removes zeros, then removes duplicate values. The first operation treats 0 as if it meant missing data, but our integer list has no missing-data marker. Zero means a measured 0 °C.

Harness currently generates only temperatures from 1 through 20. Run the sampled property. It passes because every generated value avoids the faulty zero filter. Follow the same function on a list containing only 0: what should the summary contain, and what does it return? Other check modes can expose zero sooner; this step isolates the positive-only recipe.

Read the claim “the summary keeps each recorded temperature once”. Once means one occurrence of each different value. The property compares against the distinct input values; it does not require a particular output order.

stages.title: Keep the freezing case as a named test
story: This step supplies the saved case in Laws as “a freezing reading is kept”. It requires the summary of a single 0 °C reading to contain that reading.

Use Run checks with Examples + boundaries. The function still removes zero, so the named check fails without needing random generation. Look at the two operations in Solution: removing repeated values is useful; removing a measured zero breaks our requirement.
In the earlier threshold experiment, the requirement was false. Here the requirement follows the task: report the recorded temperatures, including freezing. The implementation needs the repair.

story: The faulty starter is still present so you can first observe the full run fail. Repair unique to keep one copy of every recorded temperature, including zero, while removing repeated copies.

Use Run checks with All checks after your edit. The positive example, saved freezing example and wider generated property must pass together. Keep the wider generator; restricting it back to positive values would hide the bug again.

implementationSyntax.fsharp: In F#, |> passes a value to the next operation. List.filter keeps values whose predicate is true; <> means not equal, so x <> 0 discards zero. List.distinct keeps the first copy of each value.
implementationSyntax.typescript: In TypeScript, filter(x => x !== 0) keeps only nonzero values. new Set keeps one copy of each value; [...] spreads those values back into an array.
implementationSyntax.javascript: In JavaScript, filter(x => x !== 0) keeps only nonzero values. new Set keeps one copy of each value; [...] spreads those values back into an array.

naming: Use English phrase names for readable claims and descriptive LawSpec helpers. Keep short code names such as add, sort, xs and numbers when they make calls and recipes easier to follow. A phrase starts with "| and ends with |, without a closing quote. A law label identifies the claim; renaming it does not change what the definition checks. The compiler generates target-appropriate names.
